english.title: Fail to comply with an emergency housing prohibition order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that an emergency prohibition order under section 43 of the Housing Act 2004, had become operative in relation to specified premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), without reasonable excuse,

(A)_[used the premises]_
(B)_[permitted the premises to be used]_

in contravention of the order in that **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32 of the Housing Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
knowing that an emergency prohibition order had become operative in relation to premises
used premises in contravention of order OR

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale and a further fine not exceeding £20 for every day or part of a day on which he/she so uses the premises, or permits them to be so used, after conviction.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
